data.text:
Are review triage finding numbers stable across delta rounds?
After a delta review, the round output numbers the delta own findings 1..K (round-local), while `review triage --finding N` resolves N against the cumulative record, so a new finding the record holds at 4 is printed 1 in the round and --finding 1 marks a different finding.
_say_result enumerates res.findings from 1 regardless of the delta context; the record numbering comes from _merge_delta kept list.

evidence.note: Research CONFIRMED: _say_result numbers a delta round findings #1..#K while review triage --finding N resolves against the cumulative record (bug B32ce00713b reproduced in the regression test: round printed #1 d.py:1, record held #4).
Read the work-queue rules, r-gemini-key-load, r-task-phase-needs-wave; followed claim-before-edit and regression-test-first.

Fix in ddflow/api/review/records.py (_say_result + _record_numbers) and run.py (_delta_kept); regression test in tests/test_review_delta.py: test_a_delta_finding_is_numbered_by_its_place_in_the_record.

chunk_findings.detail: `delta_kept` is computed once before the reviewer loop and passed unchanged to every `_say_result(say, res, delta_kept)` call. `_record_numbers` numbers each reviewer's new findings starting from `horizon = len(kept)`, but it never incorporates the findings already emitted by earlier reviewers in the same delta round. Concrete failure: a delta gate with no prior findings (`kept == []`) and two reviewers, each returning one new finding. Reviewer 1's output prints `#1`; reviewer 2's output also prints `#1`, because both calls use an empty `kept`. When the round is recorded, reviewer 1's finding is record #1 and reviewer 2's is record #2, so `review triage --finding 1` addresses reviewer 1's finding rather than reviewer 2's, reproducing the exact wrong-triage bug the change is meant to fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/run.py:615 and ddflow/api/review/records.py:_record_numbers

chunk_findings.detail: `run_cli(repo, "task", "add", "T1", "--title", "add files", "--globs", "*.py")` creates task `T1` without `--phase`, `--needs`, or `--wave`. This violates [r-task-phase-needs-wave], which requires every task to name a phase, state dependencies, and carry a `wave:N` tag (`no-deps` when there is no prerequisite). As written, the fixture task has no wave tag, so `ddflow waves --stamp` cannot stamp it.

chunk_findings.detail: If the gate has no prior `chunk_findings` (for example, the first delta review of a gate), `_delta_kept` returns `None`. `_say_result` then takes the `kept is None` branch and numbers each reviewer’s findings from `1`, so with two reviewers the second reviewer’s finding is printed as `#1`. The record after the round contains both reviewers’ findings as entries 1 and 2 — the list `review triage --finding N` addresses — so a user who saw the second reviewer’s output as `#1` and runs `review triage --finding 1` marks the first reviewer’s finding instead. Delta mode should use an empty list when `chunk_findings` is absent, not `None`, so the first reviewer’s new findings seed the kept list for later reviewers.
chunk_findings.title: run.py:_delta_kept

chunk_findings.detail: The guard `if kind != "delta" or it is None: return None` means a full round still passes `kept=None` to `_say_result`, so `_record_numbers` renumbers each reviewer from `#1` separately. The same `for` loop over `revs` allows a full round to have more than one reviewer. Given a full review with reviewer A finding `a1` and reviewer B finding `b1`, reviewer B’s first finding is printed as `#1`, but in the cumulative record it is after A’s finding; `review triage --finding 1` then still targets A’s finding instead of the one the agent saw under B. That is the same B32ce00713b mismatch in a non-delta round, so the fix is incomplete for full multi-reviewer rounds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/run.py:_delta_kept

chunk_findings.detail: `_record_numbers` mutates the `kept` list in-place (`kept.append(...)`), but `_delta_kept` in `run.py` copies the list via `list(kept)` only for the initial state. When multiple reviewers run in the same delta round (as tested in `test_two_reviewers_delta_findings_are_numbered_across_the_record`), the first reviewer mutates the shared `delta_kept` list, which contaminates the state for subsequent reviewers in the same round, causing subsequent reviewers to incorrectly skip or misalign findings if digests match across reviewers.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:65

data.probe: B32ce00713b is delta rounds renumbering findings ACROSS rounds; a full round multi-reviewer numbering is pre-existing and named by _say_triage_scope ('triage addresses REVIEWER findings #1..#N'), not this change (which scopes to kind==delta). Fixing the full round would change 20 existing test expectations in test_review_triage.py:test_with_two_reviewers_the_recorded_ones_findings_are_named.
data.title: ddflow/api/review/run.py:_delta_kept

data.probe: the mutation is intentional: _record_numbers extends the shared kept list so each later reviewer finding takes the next record number (the fix). When digests match across reviewers the record dedupes them (_merge_delta have map), so sharing one number is correct, not a misalignment.

chunk_findings.detail: The added guard `if kind != "delta" or it is None: return None` still leaves the same triage mismatch for a full review round with more than one reviewer. For example, a full review (`kind` is not `"delta"`) on a gate with no prior record and two reviewers where reviewer 1 returns finding A and reviewer 2 returns finding B: `_delta_kept` returns `None`, so `_say_result` calls `_record_numbers(res, None)` and prints B as `#1`. The record saved after the round still has both findings as entries 1 and 2 (the list `review triage --finding N` addresses), so `review triage --finding 1` marks A, not the B the user just saw printed as `#1`. The new docstring’s claim that a full round’s “own numbering is already the record’s” is false whenever more than one reviewer reports in the same full round.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/run.py:_delta_kept

chunk_findings.detail: The test is cited as the probe for the confirmed HIGH (first delta review with no prior `chunk_findings`, where `_delta_kept` returns `None` and two reviewers are each numbered from `#1`), but it never reaches that condition: it calls `_review(repo)` before the delta, so the gate already has a full-round record and `_delta_kept` will find prior `chunk_findings`. In the actual buggy environment — two reviewers, a fresh gate, and no prior record — the buggy branch produces the duplicated `#1`s, while this test's delta takes the prior-record branch and would still pass. The no-prior first-delta failure mode is the exact reported defect and remains unexercised by this regression test.
